lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\UserVO\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
35 uses of the private API of the server in 5 files. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

Nothing in the app calls 2 routes outside OCS. Looked for: a route name or a path in the PHP source and the templates, in 5 files of the frontend source and in the navigation of info.xml. A route stays behind when the frontend stops calling it. A route that only a client outside the app calls shows here as well, unless its method allows requests from other origins (CORS).
vimeo/psalm is in require-dev of composer.json. The manual recommends a vendor-bin/ of bamarni/composer-bin-plugin per tool, so that the dependencies of a tool cannot conflict with those of the app.

34 inline styles in templates/. The default Content Security Policy of the server allows inline style; a response whose policy disallows it drops them. A stylesheet added with OCP\Util::addStyle() holds in both cases.

1 transaction is opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.

3 timed jobs do not say whether they are time sensitive. A job that sets TIME_INSENSITIVE with setTimeSensitivity() is moved to the maintenance window of the server; whether a job is heavy enough for that only its maintainer knows.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 7 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 41 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
